# Section 020: Networking And Storage

The reader connects workloads safely and gives them storage: traffic enters through the Gateway API, NetworkPolicy allows only the flows a workload needs, and PersistentVolumeClaims get storage from a StorageClass on demand. It follows compute because a placed workload is what these objects connect and attach to.

**Curriculum item covered:** Applying Platform Architecture Best Practices for Networking, Storage, and Compute

---

## What You Will Master

- Name the roles of GatewayClass, Gateway and HTTPRoute and which team owns each
- Create a Gateway listener and attach an HTTPRoute to it with parentRefs
- Route requests by path and by header to two backend Services
- Split traffic between two backends with backendRefs weights
- Diagnose a route that does not attach from its status.parents conditions (Accepted, ResolvedRefs)
- Allow a route from another namespace with allowedRoutes and a ReferenceGrant where needed
- Apply a default-deny ingress and egress policy to a namespace and prove that requests now time out
- Allow one flow between two workloads with podSelector and ports
- Allow traffic from another namespace with namespaceSelector, and tell apart AND versus OR selector combinations
- Restore DNS for selected pods with an egress rule to kube-dns on port 53 UDP and TCP
- Diagnose which policy blocks a request by listing the policies that select a pod
- Read a StorageClass's provisioner, reclaimPolicy, volumeBindingMode and allowVolumeExpansion fields
- Create a PersistentVolumeClaim and explain why it stays Pending under WaitForFirstConsumer until a pod uses it
- Mount a claim in a pod and prove that data survives a pod restart
- Choose an access mode (ReadWriteOnce, ReadOnlyMany, ReadWriteMany, ReadWriteOncePod) for a workload
- Predict what happens to the volume when a claim is deleted under Delete and Retain reclaim policies
- Set the default StorageClass with the is-default-class annotation

## The Learning Path

### 1. Route Traffic With The Gateway API
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 1: Route Traffic With The Gateway API](./module-01/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-020/module-01/playground` — Single-node kind cluster with the Gateway API standard CRDs and a Gateway API controller from the astrona `gatewayAPI` addon (plumbing; read the GatewayClass name from the cluster). Namespace `starfleet` with `bridge` (nginx), `scout` and `probe` Services and `shuttle`. Namespace `outpost` with its own `probe`. No Gateway or HTTPRoute yet. Requests are sent from `shuttle` to the Gateway's in-cluster Service address, or through kubectl port-forward, because kind has no load balancer.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS017.git -c sections/section-020/module-01/playground
    ```

### 2. Isolate Traffic With NetworkPolicy
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 2: Isolate Traffic With NetworkPolicy](./module-02/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-020/module-02/playground` — Single-node kind cluster (kind's default CNI kindnet enforces NetworkPolicy since kind v0.24.0). Namespaces `starfleet` (`scout`, `probe`, `shuttle`) and `outpost` (`probe`, a second `shuttle`), each namespace labelled with kubernetes.io/metadata.name. No NetworkPolicy at all, so every request succeeds at the start and the reader sees each policy remove traffic.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS017.git -c sections/section-020/module-02/playground
    ```

### 3. Provision Storage With StorageClasses
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 3: Provision Storage With StorageClasses](./module-03/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-020/module-03/playground` — Single-node kind cluster with kind's default StorageClass `standard` (rancher.io/local-path, WaitForFirstConsumer). A second StorageClass `standard-retain` with reclaimPolicy Retain. Namespace `starfleet` with `shuttle` and no PersistentVolumeClaims. A `probe` StatefulSet manifest with volumeClaimTemplates is ready to apply.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS017.git -c sections/section-020/module-03/playground
    ```

### Section Capstone Challenge
*   **Comprehensive Challenge:** Networking And Storage Capstone — `sections/section-020/capstone/labs/lab-01` *(created in the build phase)*
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS017.git -c sections/section-020/capstone/labs/lab-01
    astrona submit -c .
    ```
*   **Hands-on Objective:** `starfleet` must expose `bridge` through a Gateway, routing /api to `scout`, while a default-deny policy blocks everything except the gateway-to-workload flows and DNS; `scout` must also keep its data on a PersistentVolumeClaim from the Retain StorageClass. The reader builds the Gateway and HTTPRoute, the NetworkPolicies and the claim, and proves each with requests from `shuttle` and data that survives a pod restart.
